info.title: say API
info.summary: HTTP API currently implemented by say
info.description: OpenAPI collection for the implemented authentication, season, ledger, reconciliation, and market-registry HTTP APIs. Import this file into Postman, then edit the server URL for your deployment. Authenticate using the `say_session` cookie or an Authorization Bearer token. Browser authentication uses an HttpOnly, Secure, SameSite=Lax cookie. Mobile clients may use Bearer authentication. Public market and season routes need no credentials. Admin routes require a valid session and role-based authorization described on each operation. Order admission, authenticated order reads, public book/trade/history reads, and cancellation are included below. The WebSocket stream remains a separate runtime surface and is not specified here. Timestamps are RFC 3339; season display timezone is Africa/Lagos. Amounts and prices are integer play-money units unless stated otherwise.

get.description: Public liveness probe. Confirms the process is serving without querying dependencies.
Public readiness probe. Checks configured dependencies and returns only check status, never dependency error details.

503.description: One or more dependencies are unavailable or the service is shutting down.

get.description: Public signup step. Rate-limited to 60 checks per minute per IP. Username matching is case-insensitive.

post.description: Public signup step. Reserves an available username for ten minutes. Use the returned hold_id in signup or Google completion.
Signup step 2. Sends a six-digit email verification code. Keep signup_token for OTP resend and verification; it expires after 30 minutes. Rate limit: five signups per IP per hour.

For email verification, send signup_token and purpose=verify_email. For password reset, send email and purpose=reset_password; the response does not disclose whether the email exists. A resend is available at most once per 60 seconds and five times per email per hour.
Signup step 3. On success, sets the say_session cookie. Codes expire after ten minutes and lock after five incorrect attempts.

post.summary: Log in with email and password
post.description: Sets the say_session cookie on success. Mobile clients may also read the session token from Set-Cookie and use Authorization: Bearer.

get.description: Redirects to Google. intent defaults to login; signup begins Google signup; link requires a valid session and links Google to that account.

Google redirects to this endpoint. The API redirects back to the configured app URL. Outcomes include /, /signup/google?pending_token=…&email=…, /settings?google=linked, or /login?error=CODE. Successful sign-in sets the session cookie.

302.description: Redirect back into the application; may set say_session.

post.description: Completes signup for a new Google identity after the user picks a held username. Sets the session cookie.
Idempotent and allowed without a session. Revokes the current session when present and clears the say_session cookie.
Requires a session. Revokes every other session for the account while preserving the current session.
Always responds with 202 and an empty object to avoid disclosing whether an email address is registered.
Ends every active session and clears the current session cookie.

delete.description: Flags the account as deleted, ends all sessions, and clears the cookie. The operation is accepted asynchronously.

get.summary: List seasons available to market administration
get.description: Requires a valid session and creator or reviewer market access. Only ACTIVE and SCHEDULED seasons are returned.

200.description: Season choices for the market form.

get.description: Requires a valid session and creator or reviewer market access.

post.description: Requires a valid session and creator/reviewer access. New sources are unapproved by default and cannot validate a market until approved through the configured governance workflow.

Requires a session and a UUID Idempotency-Key. Admission and holds commit atomically. The handler waits up to 300ms for committed execution, returning 200 with the private order or 202 ADMITTED. Identical retries return the same order even after closure; changing intent conflicts. Account, owner, holds and sequence facts are server-owned.

200.description: Committed execution, including resting or rejected results. Includes private order fields, command_id and existing.

get.description: Requires a session. Only the owning account can read the order; missing and non-owned order IDs both return 404. Response is no-store.

delete.description: Requires a session and ownership. Cancellation is durably queued; 202 means pending, not yet committed. Repeating the request returns the existing command.

200.description: Committed cancellation or current final order for the existing cancel command.

get.description: Requires a session. Uses bounded keyset pagination. status defaults to open and can be all; market_id is optional. Cursor is bound to account, market filter, and status. Response is no-store.
Public, immutable in-memory view. A non-ready, expired, or unavailable local view returns 503; no actor message is sent.
Returns fills in descending execution sequence and fill index. Cursor is market-scoped; limit defaults to 50 and is capped at 100.
Returns minute-price OHLCV bars downsampled to at most about 120 buckets for 1H, 6H, 1D, 1W, or ALL.
